_help: F-27: the named people of the world (scripts/NpcDb.cs loads, scripts/NpcSchedule.cs runs their days). File order = stable index (NpcRec.Idx). area: town | road | wild. town: a POI id (village = Oakhaven, else <land>_<place>). Spots: {house:n} = house n of the town (block houses in build order; house 0 is the town's inn unless towns.<id>.inn says otherwise), {dx,dz} = offset in the town's (or poi's) frame, {x,z} = world point, poi = another POI's frame. schedule: a template name below (+ shift hours) or a list of {from,to,act,place}; hours 0-24, a range may wrap past midnight. act: sleep (hidden at the place), eat, work, socialize, patrol, travel. place: home, work, inn, square, patrol (a round of towns.<id>.patrol metres), road (route: road n of a land, between fractions from..to; 'home' = the Verdant Isle). wander: metres round the work spot. talk: the dialogue role of the old NPCs (quest, shop, smith, arena, pettrader, valor, talk); merchants and smiths of role talk get their trade in the dialog. Existing quest NPCs (data/quests.json) keep position, lines and quests there; here they get their schedule and personality.

greetings: Come closer, child. My eyes are not what they were.
The stones hummed again last night. You felt it too, didn't you?
Coin for goods, goods for coin.
Back again? I saved you something.
Keep your blade sharp.
Quiet watch so far. Don't change that.
A good edge is worth more than a good story.
Mind the sparks.
Blood, sand and applause!
The crowd is hungry today, hero.
Every cube hums with a different soul.
Shh. Listen. Your pets are happy today.
Valor earned is valor spent. Let us see your tally.
The quartermaster is open for business.
Welcome to Oakhaven, stranger.
Heard the latest? No? Well...
The arena folk are loud but they pay well.
Fine weather for it, whatever it is.
Moon looks wrong some nights.
Oh! Didn't see you there.
Come in out of the wind, love. Stew's on.
Sit anywhere. Not there, that's Tomas's chair.
Mornin'! Mind the furrows.
Smell that soil. Best on the isle.
Aye.
Good day for ploughing, this.
Evening. Move along.
Lantern's lit. You're safe enough.
Fresh loaves! Still warm!
Try a honey cake, first one's free. Well. Half free.
Shh. Tracks.
Wolves were by here an hour ago.
You stand in Wintermere Keep. Kindly wipe your boots.
State your business; the steward listens.
Stand straight when you speak to me.
The walls hold. So do I.
Ha! Another sword arm. Let's see your steel!
Cold out, hot in here. Best place in the keep.
Broth's hot. Bowls are over there.
You look half frozen. Sit.
Cold night. Keep moving.
Nothing gets past Ulf. Mostly.
Shut the door, quick! Warmth is dear up here.
A song for the hearth? No? Cider then.
Furs. Best north of the bridge.
You want warm? I have warm.
Fresh snow. Good tracking.
Out of my light.
Halt! Oh. You're a traveller. Welcome!
All is well in Hollowfrost, citizen.
Hm.
Wood's split. Need some?
Speak, or let me work.
Steel remembers every blow.
Snowbell and frostcap, a cure for most griefs.
Mind the jars; some of them bite.
Name. Business.
Keep your weapon sheathed in Rimeholt.
Have you met Bluebell? She's the one eating your bag.
Goat cheese? Best on the mountain!
The sun favours you, traveller. Perhaps I shall too.
Kesh Amaran rewards the useful. Are you useful?
Spices from beyond the dunes! Smell, smell!
For you, a special price. Very special.
A rug is a story you may stand upon.
Sit. Tea first. Business after.
Shade and water for the weary.
Every guest brings a little of the desert in. Shake it off.
Peace within the walls of Kesh.
The city watch sees all, stranger.
Out late? So am I.
Night's the honest time in Kesh. Everyone shows their face.
Walk in peace.
The stars are bright tonight. A good sign.
Hmph. Show me the blade.
Good steel, poor care. Typical.
The sun rises for all, even for you.
Light a candle, child. The dead are listening.
Water first, then talk. Drink!
Another caravan? Bless the oasis.
Dates are sweet this year.
The palms remember my father's hands.
Nothing ever happens here. Please keep it that way.
Psst. Got any cards?
Water skins! Fresh from the oasis!
Going into the dunes? You'll want two of these.
Wipe your feet. Not that it'll help.
Eel stew or nothing. It's always eel stew.
The mist is thick; the fish are thicker.
Don't follow the little lights. Never the lights.
Stay on the boards.
Something moved in the reeds. Probably a heron.
Heh. A fresh face. Want to keep it fresh? I have a salve.
Bog myrtle cures what ails you. Mostly.
Eels! Smoked eels! Er, do you like eels?
Buying? Selling? Both? Please?
Reeds for roofs, reeds for baskets, reeds for everything!
Watch your step, the boards are slick.
Bog iron, best there is. Don't let anyone tell you different.
Need a hinge? Everyone needs a hinge.
Boards only. No wading.
Reedholm. Behave.
Sit, and I'll tell you what sleeps under the water.
The bastion bells rang last night. There are no bells.
Ashford steel! Hardest in the highlands!
You hold that sword like a spoon.
Coin on the bar, love, then we're friends.
Whisky's smoky, harp's out of tune, and you're welcome.
Obsidian, ash-glass, ember-salt. What may I offer?
Prices are fair. Stock is fresh. Time is short.
Ah, armour? Let me measure you. Hold still. Stiller.
Every ring matters. Every single one.
Ashford's watch is at your service, within reason.
Do not make me regret your presence.
Evening! Lovely glow off the mountain tonight.
Stay where the lamps are, friend.
Keep moving.
Ashford watch. Any trouble, find me.
May the hearth-flame keep you.
Are you hurt? The flame mends more than it burns.
You may approach. Briefly.
Cinderhold has stood for nine hundred years. Do not be the reason it falls.
What.
If you're looking for trouble, you've found the wrong captain.
Who goes— oh. Good evening.
Did you feel the ground shake? Just me? Right.
Hungry? Course you are. Everyone is in this cold stone pile.
Sit, eat, and tell me everything.
Forge is hot, prices are hotter.
His lordship pays late. You'll pay up front.
Welcome to the Ember Hearth. It's small, but it's warm.
Any news from the keep?
Ash makes good soil. Odd, but true.
Peppers are coming in hot this year.
The mountain glows like a heart tonight.
Halt, and admire the sky with me a moment.
Ooh, a new face! Buying or browsing?
Fire-salt, charms, rope. Everything a hero needs!
Ah. A visitor. Do mind the scrolls.
History is a river, friend. We are merely the current.
Silk spun under the moon. Touch it gently.
Quality is quiet. It needs no shouting.
Welcome to the Silver Bough. A song or a cup?
Rest your feet, wanderer. The night is young.
Potions. Tested. Mostly.
You. Bring me a wyrm scale and I'll make it worth your while.
The Silver Watch greets you.
Aurelion's peace is old. Help us keep it.
The owls and I keep watch. The owls are better at it.
Late wanderer? I won't tell.
The stars wheel; I watch.
Walk softly; the city dreams.
Each blade I make is a poem in steel.
You may admire. Touching costs extra.
Peace, child. The oak remembers you.
Every root drinks from the same water.
Have you seen my pumpkins? Biggest in the vale!
Pie at the inn tonight. Pumpkin, naturally.
Tea's brewing. Sit if you like.
If Perrin asks, you've already seen the pumpkins.
Evening, young one. Mind the frost.
Forty years I've walked this round. Still the prettiest village.
Ribbons, buttons, a secret or two. Interested?
I hear things. Things cost.
Horseshoe? Hinge? Hammer? I do 'em all.
Easy now. No rush in Mossbrook.
Good day. Mossbrook welcomes peaceful folk.
Report anything strange near the caverns.
Oh, um, hello. Honey? It's good honey.
The bees like you. That's... good, I think.
Moss grows where the world is patient.
Breathe. The vale breathes with you.
Lovely day for walking! Every day is.
Heading to the barrow? Rather you than me!
Cart's full, purse is light. Buy something?
Turnip doesn't bite. Usually.
Road's clear to the bend. After that, eyes open.
Goblins hit a cart here last week.
Hauling grain to the causeway. Again.
If you see a loose wheel, it's mine.
The road is home.
Water. Shade. Then talk.
Walk with me a while, if you like.
Every shrine is a door left open.
Can't stop. Letters.
Urgent post for Rimeholt. Out of the way, please.
Keep to the road; the snow hides holes.
Wintermere's that way. Don't dawdle.
Wicker baskets! Waterproof! Mostly!
Don't go near the bastion. I'm not saying why.
Ho there! Road's safe, thanks to yours truly.
Race you to the Throat? No? Pity.
The stones sing tonight. Can you hear their verse?
Go back, or go through. Do not linger.
Timber! Ha, just kidding. Hello!
Skeletons don't bother me. I've got an axe.
Quiet. The drake hears everything.
One day I'll put an arrow in its eye.
Peace be upon you, pilgrim.
I keep the candle lit, so the deep fire stays deep.
Welcome to the fire of the Sandstriders.
Sit. In the desert, a guest is sacred.
N-no further! The kings are sleeping!
You're not a robber, are you? You have robber eyes.
Cold enough for you?
Something big lives in the maw. Don't wake it.
Found a ring this morning. Not selling. Unless...
The bastion gives up treasure at low tide. And sometimes bodies.
Listen! The Throat is singing today!
Mind the cracks, they're hotter than they look.
The roots told me you were coming.
Step lightly; the ground is listening.

_help_reputation: F-28 (scripts/NpcMemory.cs): what NPCs remember and how standing moves. Standing with an NPC and with a town runs -100..100. Prices use npcWeight x NPC standing + townWeight x town standing: at +100 buying is priceMax cheaper and selling pays priceMax more, at -100 the reverse. At or below refuseBelow an NPC will not trade, smith or give quests. tiers: lowest standing of each name. gifts: one per NPC per giftEvery seconds played; a gift is any pack material; liked / disliked by role lists ('*' at the end = any id starting so, 'default' = every role) or when a word of the NPC's own likes / dislikes is in the gift's name. memory_lines: the opening line by what the NPC remembers ({name} = the hero, {gift} = the last gift, {town}); '<situation>.<speech>' overrides for one speech style.

first: We have not met. {me}, at your service.
first.nervous: Oh! H-hello. I'm {me}. Have we met? No. No, we haven't.
first.formal: We have not been introduced. I am {me}.
first.sly: Well, well. A stranger. They call me {me}.
first.poetic: A new traveller on the old road. I am called {me}.
first.warm: Welcome, stranger. I'm {me}. Come, don't be shy.
liked: Good to see you, {name}. Folk here speak well of you.
{name}! I was hoping you would come by.
trusted: {name}, my friend. For you, my door is always open.
There are few I trust in {town}, {name}. You are one.
trusted.gruff: {name}. You, I'd share a fire with.
hated: You have nerve, showing your face here.
Get away from me, {name}. I have nothing for you.
gift: I still have the {gift} you gave me, {name}. That was kind.
gift.gruff: The {gift}. Hm. Was good of you.
badgift: Come to hand me more {gift}? Keep it.
I have not forgotten the {gift}, {name}. I wish I could.
insult: I remember what you called me, {name}.
insult.nervous: P-please don't say those things again, {name}.
crime: I saw what you did. Don't think I've forgotten.
Keep your hands where I can see them, {name}.
quest: {name}! After what you did for us, you are always welcome here.
We have not forgotten your help, {name}.
quest.gruff: You did the job, {name}. I remember that.
trade: My best customer! What will it be today, {name}?
refuse: I will not deal with the likes of you.
Not for you. Not after what you've done.
took.liked: For me? Oh, {gift}! You remembered what I like.
{gift}! How did you know? Thank you, {name}.
took.neutral: That's thoughtful of you. Thank you.
took.disliked: I... suppose it's the thought that counts. It is not.
took.soon: You have given me enough for one day, {name}. Keep it.
insulted.sly: Careful. I collect debts, and that is one.

_help_social: F-29 / F-30 (scripts/NpcSocial.cs): the short lines shown as speech bubbles above heads, and when. chats: two NPCs within chatDist metres (or socializing within approachDist: one walks over) stop, face each other and trade lines; a chat is a list of [speaker 0 or 1, line]. gossip is the usual kind, argue when one's likes meet the other's dislikes (or argueChance), trade when one of them is a trader, pass when one is only walking by. {other} = the other's first name, {like} / {dislike} = one of the speaker's own, {town}, {name} = the hero. onlooker: someone near an argument. act.<activity>: said when the schedule moves on. rain / rainstop / dawn / dusk / night: reactions to weather and the time of day. player.<standing>: said to the hero walking up (by what the NPC remembers, F-28); unknown heroes get one of the NPC's own greetings.

gossip: Did you hear about the lights over the barrow?
They say a hero's been seen about {town}.
Your knees said snow last week.
Have you seen the price of bread?
Strange folk on the road lately.
I dreamt of the Rift again.
If I never see {dislike} again, it'll be too soon.
argue: You and your {like}. I can't stand it.
Better than {dislike}, which is all YOU bring.
We'll see what the guard says.
I don't see your name on it.
trade: For you? The best I have.
For you? The worst I have.
Two for the price of one?
One for the price of two. Final offer.
onlooker.guard: Break it up. Both of you.
act.sleep: That's me done for the day.
rain: And I just hung the washing!
My hat is not built for this.
rain.guard: Rain or shine, the watch stands.
rain.fisher: Fish bite best in the wet.
night: Should be indoors, the lot of us.
player.hated: Guards have their eye on you.
player.night: You'll catch your death out here.
player.rain: Dreadful weather to be wandering in.
